notice: Paraphrases are working notes, not quotations, and every entry is UNREVIEWED until an attorney checks it against the opinion and current treatment. No outcome percentages are computed from this corpus.

issues.disposition: complaint held insufficient; court of appeals reversed
issues.paraphrase: Parallel conduct, without further factual context suggesting a preceding agreement, does not plausibly allege a Section 1 conspiracy. No probability requirement is imposed at the pleading stage.

authorities.name: NCAA v. Alston

issues.paraphrase: The degree of scrutiny (per se, abbreviated, or full rule of reason) depends on the restraint and its context; market analysis is not identical across Section 1 theories.

authorities.note: Labor-side restraint: doctrine noted for framework selection only.

authorities.name: SD3, LLC v. Black & Decker (U.S.) Inc.

issues.defendant_scope: manufacturer defendants alleged to have participated in the boycott
issues.paraphrase: Allegations are assessed as a whole; the complaint alleged the who, what, when and where of the boycott agreement.

issues.defendant_scope: corporate affiliates and other defendants for whom no participation facts were alleged
issues.paraphrase: Corporate affiliation alone does not plead a given entity's participation in the conspiracy.
Separate conspiracy theories are tested separately.

authorities.name: In re Text Messaging Antitrust Litigation

issues.paraphrase: Parallel pricing together with alleged industry structure, trade-association information exchange and price increases in the face of falling costs was held enough to plead agreement.

authorities.note: Summary judgment for defendants was later affirmed, 782 F.3d 867 (7th Cir. 2015): a pleading-stage ruling and a merits ruling are recorded separately.

authorities.name: In re Musical Instruments & Equipment Antitrust Litigation

issues.paraphrase: Alleged plus factors (common motive, similar policies adopted over time, trade-association attendance) were held consistent with independent self-interested conduct.

authorities.name: Anderson News, L.L.C. v. American Media, Inc.

issues.paraphrase: At the pleading stage the court does not choose between two plausible inferences from the facts alleged.

authorities.name: Mayor & City Council of Baltimore v. Citigroup, Inc.

issues.paraphrase: Parallel conduct that each defendant had an evident independent business reason to take did not plausibly suggest agreement.

authorities.name: Brown Shoe Co. v. United States

issues.paraphrase: Product-market boundaries turn on reasonable interchangeability and cross-elasticity; submarkets may be identified by practical indicia.

authorities.note: Merger case: cited for market-definition method only.

authorities.name: Ohio v. American Express Co.

issues.paraphrase: Two-sided transaction platforms may require a single market spanning both sides.

authorities.note: Extension point only: two-sided platforms are out of scope for v1 schemas.
